transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

That pulsing sound is usually the vacuum's protection system kicking in because airflow is restricted or a sensor detects an issue. Since the battery is charged, the most common cause is a clogged filter that hasn't been washed recently, or a filter that was washed but not left to dry for 24 hours (even slight dampness can trigger this). Please check if you have washed the filters lately and ensure they are bone-dry before trying again.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. never washed the filter tbh, didnt know u could. no burning smell or heat tho. how do i wash it

On the V8 Animal, there are two filters: one pre-motor filter (usually blue) near the bin and a post-motor HEPA filter at the back of the motor housing. To wash them, pull both out, rinse thoroughly under cold running water until it runs clear, shake off the excess water, and leave them to dry completely for 24 hours in a warm room.
ok washed it, water came out black lol. left it overnight on the radiator. pulses way less now but still a bit

It’s good that washing the filters helped – black water shows they were very clogged, which restricts airflow and causes the pulsing. There is likely a remaining blockage in the airway (hose, wand, or floorhead) or the filters are not 100% dry yet (radiator drying can sometimes leave the core damp even if the outside feels dry). Please check for physical obstructions first: detach all parts and look through the wand and into the bin inlet to ensure nothing is stuck. If everything looks clear, let the filters dry in a warm, airy place for another 12–24 hours before testing again.
ok checked the wand, big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

That’s excellent news – removing the blockage has sorted it. To stop this happening again, try to empty the bin and check for hair tangles every few uses, as that clump of cat litter was clearly choking the airflow. Just give those filters a quick rinse if they get dark again in future. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
